subject: Runway uplift request — short trial safeguard vs. credit top-up
messages:
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@cedarpoint.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@cedarpoint.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway uplift request — short trial safeguard vs. credit top-up

Hi Hannah,

Quick note from our side — the team is seeing faster-than-expected burn on the shorttrial (mostly Transformer-heavy inference on long contexts). We have two asks before we can sign-off on conversion: 1) an extra 2–3 weeks of access to the dedicated eval window or 2) a credit top-up to cover the additional tokens so we can finish the final integration tests.

We prefer the extra time (ops has dependencies), but procurement will likely push for a credit-based solution. Can Redwood surface a compact bridging option that doesn't require a full PO amendment?

I attached the latest burn report.

Thanks —
Ayesha
Sr. ML Engineer, CedarPoint Analytics

Attachments: cedarpoint_poc_burn_report.pdf (pdf, 340 KB)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@cedarpoint.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway uplift request — short trial safeguard vs. credit top-up

Ayesha — thanks for the context and the burn snapshot, useful. Two quick clarifications: which of your workloads are driving the longest contexts (inference vs. eval), and is there a hard deadline for a go/no-go decision?

High level response: we can do either approach. Short-term we typically offer either (A) a 14-day runway extension with the same access pattern and a cap on engineering support hours, or (B) a one-time credit top-up tied to the trial that shows up on your next invoice. Option A needs an addendum signed; option B can be done more quickly but procurement often wants the dollar value up front.

Looping in Ben for pricing and Kimberly for legal/PO flow — Ben, can you propose a compact offer that balances procurement friction and CedarPoint's preference for extra time?

Best,
Hannah
Head of Commercial — Trials & Pilots, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway uplift request — short trial safeguard vs. credit top-up

Hannah / Kimberley — drafting an offer now. Proposed compact options for CedarPoint: 

- Offer 1 (Timebox extension): 14 additional days on the existing trial window, identical resource profile, includes up to 8 hours of priority engineering support (SLO: 24-hour response). Requires signed single-page addendum ("Trial Addendum v1"). No additional dollar charge; we request the same trial SLA continued.

- Offer 2 (Credit top-up): $12,000 one-time credit applied to their account to cover token overage for the next 30 days. No change to trial end date. Procurement-friendly (can be processed as a credit memo).

Trade-offs: Offer 1 keeps the evaluation deterministic for their engineers (preferred for integration work). Offer 2 is faster for procurement and avoids legal processing time. I suggest we lead with Offer 1 (customer preference) but provide Offer 2 as an exec-approved fallback.

Attachments: proposed-addendum-v1.docx (docx)

If that works, Hannah—can you present to Ayesha and include the DocuSign link? Kimberly, if legal can pre-approve the one-page addendum we should be able to close in 1–2 business days.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@cedarpoint.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@cedarpoint.ai>, procurement@cedarpoint.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway uplift request — short trial safeguard vs. credit top-up

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear options. Ops prefers Offer 1 (14 days + 8 hrs support) because our integration requires the live window. Procurement asked whether the addendum can explicitly call out: 1) no changes to existing data handling terms, 2) a single auto-expire clause at the end of the extension, and 3) a one-time SLA credit of 5% if we see a service availability breach during the extension.

If you can accept those bullets, procurement will sign quickly. If not, procurement will push for Offer 2 (credit) since their process is faster.

Ayesha

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@cedarpoint.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, procurement@cedarpoint.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway uplift request — short trial safeguard vs. credit top-up

Ayesha / Tom / Procurement — thanks. Quick update and decision path: 

1) Legal (Kimberly) confirmed we can accept the three procurement bullets with minor edits: the auto-expire language will be explicit and the SLA credit is capped at 5% of the prorated trial fee (we'll reflect that in the addendum).

2) Ben has pre-authorized the 14‑day extension and the 8‑hour support bucket. We'll attach the signed addendum and countersign via DocuSign. If procurement prefers a credit memo instead, we can issue the $12,000 credit as an alternative — note that credit processing may add 3–5 business days to the timeline.

Next steps: Hannah to send DocuSign for Addendum v1 with Kimberly's minor edits OR Ben to initiate credit memo flow if procurement requests. Please confirm preference by EOD Monday so we can keep the evaluation window continuous.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.example.com/placeholder/DEAL-004728
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4728

Looking forward —
Hannah
Head of Commercial — Trials & Pilots, Redwood Inference
